title: Where is the lesion? The nerves of the upper limb
intro: Pick a lesion of the brachial plexus or of a nerve of the arm and see what is lost. Movements and reflexes read 0 = normal, 1 = weak or reduced, 2 = lost; a sign reads 1 when it is present. The muscles list shows each affected muscle with its Latin name (red: paralysed, amber: weak). Learn which findings set two lesions apart: the triceps after a radial lesion in the axilla or at the spiral groove, the clawing after an ulnar lesion at the elbow or at the wrist.
opt1: Roots C8–T1 torn from the cord (Klumpke)
opt3: Axillary nerve in the quadrangular space
opt6: Radial nerve in the spiral groove
opt7: Posterior interosseous nerve at the supinator
opt9: Median nerve in the carpal tunnel
opt11: Ulnar nerve at the wrist (Guyon's canal)
clawLabel: Clawing of the ring and little fingers (0–1)
musclesTitle: Affected muscles (red: paralysed, amber: weak; the bar is the share of the nerve supply lost)
ladderTitle: Spinal segments: the roots that are cut are in red
